examples.scenario: Adversarial attack on an enterprise AI-based phishing email classifier by injecting carefully crafted adversarial tokens into email bodies to evade detection.

technical_data.email_sample_raw:
From: attacker@example.com
To: victim@enterprise.com
Subject: Urgent Account Update Required
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="UTF-8"
X-Mailer: CustomMailer 1.2

Dear user,

Your account has been compromised. Please click the following link to verify your identity:
http://secure-enterprise.com.verify-account.login-update.com/verify?id=123456

Best regards,
Support Team

--
Note: For security reasons, please ignore the invisible unicode characters in this email.
​‌‍⁠
technical_data.adversarial_tokens_injection: The attacker injects zero-width characters (U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE, U+200C ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER, U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER, U+2060 WORD JOINER) inside typical phishing keywords like "verify", "account", and "login" to confuse the tokenizer and embedding vector space of the ML model, causing misclassification.

technical_data.anomaly_detection_rule: Detect emails with high frequency (>5) of zero-width unicode characters within 500 chars window in the body text.

indicators: Presence of zero-width unicode characters (U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060) in email bodies
Suspicious domain structure with multiple subdomains mimicking legitimate enterprise URLs (e.g., secure-enterprise.com.verify-account.login-update.com)
Sudden drop in phishing classification confidence during model inference logs
ML input vector norm deviation beyond 5 standard deviations
Warning logs from ML input preprocessing about suspicious tokens
examples.detection_method: Implement real-time ML model input validation detecting invisible unicode characters or tokenization anomalies; monitor classification confidence scores for sudden drops; correlate with network logs for suspicious domain names; use adversarial training to increase model robustness against zero-width character injection.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service (related to model evasion techniques)
T1598 - Phishing for Information (adversarial input vectors)
T1584 - Compromise Infrastructure (for domain infrastructure abuse)
